title: Conditions for a Hindu Marriage — Section 5 HMA

content.overview: Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 states five conditions for a valid Hindu marriage: (i) neither party has a spouse living; (ii) mental capacity; (iii) ages 21 (bridegroom) and 18 (bride); (iv) not within prohibited degrees unless custom permits; (v) not sapindas unless custom permits. Breach of (i), (iv) or (v) renders the marriage void under s. 11; other breaches may lead to voidability under s. 12 or punishment under s. 18.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Living spouse? (2) Mental capacity? (3) Ages 21/18? (4) Prohibited degrees / custom? (5) Sapinda / custom? (6) Map breach to s. 11, 12 or 18?

sections.heading: Five conditions
sections.body: Monogamy; mental capacity (three sub-clauses); age 21/18; prohibited degrees (custom may save); sapinda (custom may save).

sections.heading: Custom exceptions
sections.body: Custom may save only clauses (iv) and (v). It cannot validate a bigamous marriage under (i).

sections.heading: Consequences of breach
sections.body: s. 11 void for (i)/(iv)/(v); s. 12 voidable for specified defects; ss. 17–18 penal consequences where applicable.

sections.heading: Ceremony and registration
sections.body: s. 7 ceremonies; where saptapadi is included, marriage is complete on the seventh step. s. 8 registration is evidence, not essential to validity.

sections.heading: Age and child marriage
sections.body: Age under HMA interacts with the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act; not every under-age marriage is treated as void under s. 11 in the same absolute manner as bigamy.

examples.title: All conditions satisfied
examples.body: Unmarried Hindus of sound mind, ages 25 and 22, not within prohibited degrees or sapinda — valid if ceremonies completed.

examples.title: Living spouse — void
examples.body: Second ceremony while first marriage subsists — void under s. 11 read with s. 5(i); s. 17 may also apply.

hypotheticals.question: Can custom validate a bigamous second marriage?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Custom exception applies only to prohibited degrees and sapinda, not to monogamy under s. 5(i).

misconceptions.trap: Only monogamy and age need to be stated for s. 5.
misconceptions.correction: All five conditions must be stated.

misconceptions.trap: Custom can save a bigamous marriage.

cases.name: Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India
cases.facts: Hindu husbands converted to Islam and contracted second marriages without dissolving the first.
cases.issue: Whether the second marriage is valid and constitutes bigamy.
cases.ratioDecidendi: A second marriage after conversion without dissolving the first Hindu marriage is void under s. 11 read with s. 5(i) and constitutes bigamy. Conversion does not automatically dissolve the Hindu marriage.
